text:
Russia attacked two major bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv on Monday night, with air strikes cutting water and heating supplies in parts of the Ukrainian capital, the city’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said Tuesday morning. Missiles hit the city’s Northern and Southern bridges, Klitschko said, and caused damage to critical infrastructure. “Some areas are experiencing disruptions to water and heating supplies,” he wrote on Telegram . Ukrainian officials said parts of Kyiv’s above-ground metro were also damaged. Eight bridges link the two banks of the city of around 3 million people. Several of the structures were targeted by Russian drones in October. Meanwhile, Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea for a second consecutive day , the peninsula’s Moscow-installed head Sergei Aksyonov said on Telegram , adding that traffic across the bridge had been suspended. He also said two people died in the Lininsky District following an overnight drone attack. The overnight strikes followed online talks on Monday between U.S., Ukrainian and European officials aimed at ending the war, attended by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
In an evening address on Monday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the meeting “difficult” and said more had to be done to help Ukraine defend itself against Russian ballistic missiles.
He added that Russia was receiving “dozens of missiles per month” from North Korea and warned that Moscow could launch fresh missile attacks on Ukraine overnight and into Tuesday.
